responsibility: This module is GCC’s core control-flow graph subsystem, shared across the middle end and backend, covering the representation, construction, analysis, maintenance, and transformation of CFGs for both GIMPLE and RTL. Its foundational headers and generic sources define basic blocks, edges, flag semantics, per-function CFG state, primitive block/edge mutation, profile propagation, and hook-based abstraction so generic code can operate uniformly on GIMPLE, normal RTL, and cfglayout RTL. On top of that substrate, the module provides graph analyses such as reachability, traversal orders, control dependence helpers, dominator and postdominator computation, dominator-tree walking, and the dynamic-tree support used to maintain dominance efficiently. It also owns loop discovery, loop metadata, loop analysis, and CFG-level loop rewriting utilities built from dominance and CFG structure. Representation-specific file families extend the generic layer for RTL by building CFGs from instruction streams, synchronizing CFG edits with RTL insns, cleaning up and simplifying backend control flow, reordering blocks for layout and hot/cold partitioning, and bridging tree/GIMPLE CFGs into the initial RTL CFG during expansion. Overall, this module is the place where GCC models and manipulates control flow as a graph, distinct from neighboring modules that focus on SSA values, GIMPLE semantics, or target code generation details outside CFG structure.
